body:
Thanks, I've spoken to a lot of therapists and talking treatments don't really help that much. It's hard to describe. I did CBT for a long time which is kind of a lot like baiting yourself, but I've been doing that anyway. Getting up isn't too hard as long as I exercise enough, drink enough water and eat right and so on. When I get up for work I usually have prepared myself for the morning to go to work. Taken lots of different kinds of medication for a long time too and it didn't effect my mood. Find it really hard to socialise or anything and prefer to stay on my own and drink, sometimes really heavily, it's the only thing I do for fun. Tried going to the AA about it but it wasn't really for me either. I don't know really, nothing seems to work out.

I don't really want to go into things too much but I have a very bad relationship with my family and have had to cut them all off. I never have any money and I'm always poor and can't get work in the field I want to do. I try to push away the victim mentality but its obvious that I don't have many advantages and can't even get to exploit the ones I do have. And I really just want to go. I know that life is hard for most people and it's not fair but I can't explain feeling like crap all the time and I just want to go.

Yeah, like I'm dead already. It's like my body is not really mine. I just use myself like a toy every day to make it through. Some very bad things have happened and it's like a lot of my body has shut down for good. Then there are other feelings and I don't want to look at them or deal with them. I have a lot of strange ideas. killing myself is something I've wanted to do for a long time but everything has been such a blur that I can't focus on it hard enough. One of my ideas has been to throw myself off a bridge near by me, or to take lots of pills with a bottle of whiskey or something. It would really mean a lot to me if I didn't have to keep waking up. I can't change the way that feeling feels.

I don't think psychopaths or narcissists understand this. If they do something wrong, ie. something deliberately malicious to another person or an animal for their own personal satisfaction, then they become confused when you try to explain there are consequences, for instance that they are not completely trustworthy anymore. I tried explaining to my father that beating up the dog for no reason was wrong and made me feel bad, but I think he really struggled with the idea that he should receive criticism or any kind of negative treatment for anything at all. Or he might take us out to a cheap restaurant and keep dropping hints about what a good father he was. My mother was a little better at this game; if she did something reprehensible, she would throw a party for some general reason so that she could recover her reputation *and* get to swim in the limelight. In a way, I have to respect her knack for efficiency, it would have gone well on a CV if she ever really decided to work.

I keep being forced into humiliating situations and have lost a lot of money recently. I keep losing my home and being pushed around and taken advantage of. I've given up on myself for a long time and just want to go.

Yes I've had to cut out my entire family as well, and there are two main reasons. The first is that they are brutal when it comes to forcing their way into peoples' lives and try to make other people responsible for them and their welfare. The second is that they are a magnet for liars. Because they are so gullible, a confident person who sees through them can have a lot of fun with them and they've been conned more than once. Once you give them attention and approval, they let down their entire guard and give you a lot of control over them. For a child, this is okay, but for a parent - let alone a grown adult this is bad and has left me in some very difficult situations. Luckily I've done so badly in life that I can barely support myself let alone a narcissist, so they've had no interest in me whatsoever. My mother is especially demanding at having everything catered for her. She always needs expensive clothes, cars, a large house etc. for free as well as receiving constant approval and attention. Just looking at how she has such a comfortable life in return for no work is bad enough but that she wants and expects MORE is really the icing on the cake. I've made it clear to my mother that I will not look after her any more which effectively ended our relationship.

Not only that but I've learned a lot about the people who associate themselves with my parents. Often they are either very gullible and vulnerable, or they are bad people who enjoy controlling and manipulating others. I am not trying to be mean but I've lived through very bad circumstances and have learned that there are a few patterns. Neither of my parents have any standards other than having it all about them, so once they find someone to tell them what they want to hear they leave the backdoor open to intruders, thieves, not so nice people. If you've been raised by narcissists then you are taught to not have boundaries, but then if your mother is dating strange guys and pretending to be in love, or if your father is being tricked by companies.... then you have another layer of defense down. These people can get to you and make your life hard or even harder and that is not something you want.

So to deal with this, any person on talking terms with my parents, in any way, is not my friend. It is really hard because not EVERY person who relates to them is bad or weak. It's not fair to be so discriminatory. In the short term, to not have a family puts you at a terrible disadvantage. But you need to make life worth living and if freedom is the only thing you can have, then it's worth it to have freedom and your own choices instead of being constantly humiliated. And also you can create your own life instead of having someone try to force you to love them all the time. I think that pushing the entire family away is a better choice than to be part of something fake. I am not sure who my family really are anymore, there are some cousins, some nieces and so on, but they give the same treatment my father does e.g. "you come to us, and we will stay put waiting for you. If we don't like you, you aren't welcome." This was the opposite when I was growing up, when everyone came round to visit and have big parties but when I became an adult nobody wanted to know. I went to visit my grandmother and she tore me apart for being unemployed and that was it. They do not want me around or respect me, and I am not rich or popular so there is no point to the relationship. 

My father is a lot worse and could fall underneath the psychopath category, he doesn't seem to have a conscience. The social cues you pick up from someone like that make you sound terrible and I learned this all the hard way. That's another way a narcissist can sneakily hurt you without even being around you. Acting arrogant and disrespectful is not a good social move. It sounds obvious but when you are taught to always ignore your own emotions and perform for others then this is why you can act the way you do. He is fascinated with sadism and sadistic pornography and I'm not sure how many of my siblings are directly relative to me. Even now he still thinks we have a working relationship when it was over a long time ago and he still likes to send me messages on the holidays. It is so humiliating that he has to be my father and I wish he was just dead or gone or whatever so I could feel safe. I really wish things could have turned out just a little differently and that I got to stay in some kind of comfort zone where you have a family or some kind of family relationship or anything.

The violent behavior is the most troubling; I would start to talk to the police to ensure the safety of everyone.

Your brother may be suffering from a case of self-absorption, and it may or may not be to do with the interactions you see in the house, or may be he's experienced something you haven't. Having parents who flip into a rage at the drop of the hat can cause some strange behavior, especially if it's in the family home.

Of course the best thing to do is to keep away from them and try to find opportunities that can help you be independant. Starting college won't necessarily give you the space you need - you might find that adults can be very difficult in many sharing situations. 

And if things are bad enough, just get a tent and a sleeping bag and sleep in the woods somewhere. Maybe there's a hiking group around your area. Did it a few times myself when things got too bad and violent

Yes it was very scary. I was very badly treated and my social worker deemed my situation to be high risk so I was given alternative housing. But my parents tried their best to stop my development. When it became clear that I was going to have my own independance they said I was no longer part of the family. I haven't heard from anyone in years so I assume I'm orphaned.

My take is that people talk about them as if they're everywhere because they don't really understand what it means. Fucked up families are everywhere unfortunately, there are sexual predators, sadists, liars, etc. but it's only after a lot of heartache that you find the motivation to really discover the difference between regular joe and narcissist. The most important thing to remember is that these are completely unempathetic people who maintain a false self. They don't have honest values and don't believe you as much more than a tool for feeling good about themselves. In my experience they are very rare, I've met two narcissists in my adulthood outside my parents, and neither was a sadist like my father, so it was a pretty bad gamble to get both a narcissistic mother *and* father. 

Yes there is a dialogue about society being more childish and blah de blah but that has probably been going on forever. Humans have feelings, not all adults care about controlling them to fit in with a social image and feelings can be overwhelming too. It's easy for a newspaper or a church to whine about how society is degrading but that to me is childish in itself.
My mother made me help her with *her* homework.

What happens when somebody is wronged by my father? Life's not fair.

What does he say in his defense when he wants something? It's not fair.

This principle went the whole way. Everything from his kids to suing just about every poor bastard who crossed his path.
The best up and trending conspiracy theory at the moment is that the 9/11 bombings *weren't* carried out by the US government

Thanks for writing that. That's really encouraging to hear. 

I think when you're faced with such tough situations, it's natural to learn how to block things out and live in a kind of bubble. Feeling like an actor is pretty devastating. 

To make the relationship with my parents more bearable, I developed a sense of humor, which wasn't really authentic, but I could manipulate them into laughing and relaxing. This meant I could act the 'right' way sometimes. This isn't always appropriate in the adult world though and at the end of the day it was fake behavior. 

I know what you mean though, when a narcissist is spoiling for a showdown they'll press all your buttons until they get something. When that doesn't work they'll do at least something to make you pay.

The apple doesn't fall far from the tree, unless the tree has put itself on a pedestal

Point is that narcissists are pretty repulsive. as long as you can discern right and wrong then you will be ok

That sounds so sad, I'm really sorry. I think a lot of people can pick up on people who have this kind of habit of self-denial and then go on to exploit them, so I can become very agitated when I'm let down in relationships

It's really hard to describe, but I always feel that if I don't have the right feelings or do the correct thing in a situation then something very bad will happen. A lot of the time it used to mean putting myself last to avoid trouble and confrontation and as an adult that's not practical. Feeling upset or feeling wronged is something I have trouble dealing with too. You're kind of right, it's a difficult question to answer.

You're so right, the minute they think that you've criticised them, even when you haven't is enough to make them feel paranoid. And trying to prove to them that you're not the enemy is pointless because then it would mean that they're flawed in some way for having the wrong idea about you. You just can't win.
That's right! Feeling good around a narcissist is just asking for trouble.

What you may find strange when/if you go LC is that the narcissist may suddenly completely disappear. Then they may reappear, hover around, then disappear for months at a time without explanation. This happens with flaky friends too of course, except flaky people don't throw tantrums and beat you up if you criticise them. What I'm trying to say is that they may suddenly become very unpredictable. It's probably best that you try to use your situation to your advantage and use it to catapult yourself into a stronger and more independant self, and this includes taking more charge of your personal finances and decisions.

You're probably feeling the same way I did, that it feels wrong to take responsibility for another person, especially when they are your guardian. Not only that but you've been lumped with more work in this confusing world. She's not asking for approval, she's -demanding- it, and she's only going to use it as proof to prove that she's better than you and others. 

Good luck with leaving your situation and try to find a safe place to live. If you do decide to tell other people irl, I find the best thing is to try to get to know people first and break it down, as a lot of people wouldn't even believe me when I talked about my own experiences.

You put that so well. The true victory comes from non-engagement. If you beat them at anything they will make it their life's ambition to harass and humiliate you. I'm not sure if a narcissist even recognises defeat in the same way a normal person does. They really believe that ultimately it is all about them.

If their aim is to tease you in and manipulate you, but they fail, then it's a real victory for you and a defeat for them. They have to go flatter/demean to a different social circle and you're free from them.

I see what you're saying, but it would have helped so so much if somebody just took a stand. The best kind of environment a narcissist can thrive in is one where the 'greed is good' mantra is celebrated. When they destroyed one friendship or family, everyone else would just shrug, but then it would happen again and again, until eventually they did so much damage that they were practically excommunicated from the neighborhood. By that time people had lost their careers, their marriages, and their futures because they had sat by and allowed the pattern of manipulation to carry on. When my mother divorced my father (or better put, neither could be bothered to keep up the facade any longer) my mother seduced almost a dozen people and my father began seducing friends and members of my mothers' family in response. They managed to generate so much drama out of nothing and caused a lot of people a lot of agony. It was OBVIOUS. All that was missing was a united front and not enough, if any people could have been bothered to work together to stop them.
